cost: recal_208's RECEIPT LOSES FOUR KNOB LINES, named here and NOT edited (recal_93's convention, recal_214's precedent): `npm run receipts -- 208` prints 45 OK / 4 missed and exits 0. The four are its ISO_VOL/ISO_EFF/ISO_JMP/ISO_FD block, its ISO_PV/ISO_PV_W block, its isoScorer line ('max(mid, 3pt) is the discriminator') and its isoScore line ('the exact mirror of heliEngineScore'). All four are the formula THIS ruling reverses, so the MISS is the record of the reversal rather than a defect. Nothing else in the ledger changes status: 25 receipts OK on 216, 0 missed.

ISO_PV_W IS GONE FROM THE SOURCE and is deliberately not receipted as an inverted knob (an absence is not a reading; a MISS fails the ledger). `git show 02f39a1:src/engine/tactics.ts | grep ISO_PV_W` is the whole of the before, and the knob line on `ISO_PV = 57` immediately followed by `ISO_BASE = -6` is the after.

ISO_PV 57 IS NOW A MEASUREMENT THAT PRICES NOTHING. It stays because recal_213's PIN_PV 56 is defined against it and a shipped test reads the pair ('it is not a synonym for iso'). It was NOT re-measured onto the new nomination: the median play volume of the man iso nominates rises with this round, and moving the constant would break that test while changing no number in the app. A later round that wants ISO_PV to mean the new median must re-open recal_213's line with it.

HIS RULING SAYS 'remove all the - across the board' AND THIS ROUND IS SCOPED TO ISO. Two other minus-shaped terms were left alone on purpose and are reported rather than touched: heliEngineScore's HELIO_PV_W (recal_206 is his own standing ruling and its content is a conjunction), and pindown's pinOffBall, which is a multiplicative FADE on play volume rather than a subtraction (PIN_PV 56 -> PIN_PV_MAX 95) and belongs to recal_213. If he means the pin-down fade too, that is its own round.

THE THINNEST MARGIN ON THE BOARD IS NOW 0.32, and it is a pinned read: the Thunder '25 keep the pick-and-roll 74.19 against iso 73.87. notes: WHAT MOVED, in one line: `isoScorer` is now ISO_VOL 0.40 x volume + ISO_EFF 0.30 x efficiency + ISO_FD 0.20 x fouldraw + ISO_MID 0.10 x mid, and `isoScore` is that composite with nothing taken off it. Per point of attribute, measured over all 10,000 cards: volume +0.40 (100% of cards) · efficiency +0.30 (100%) · fouldraw +0.20 (100%) · mid +0.10 (100%) · 3pt 0.00 (0%) · playvol 0.00 (0%). Before the round it was volume +0.40 · efficiency +0.20 · mid +0.16 (64%) · fouldraw +0.15 · playvol -0.13 (28%) · 3pt +0.09 (37%).

THE SUM MUST STAY 1, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A HOUSE PREFERENCE. The obvious reading of 'add small mid bonus' is to shrink the jumper weight and leave the other three where they are (0.40 / 0.20 / 0.15 + 0.10, sum 0.85). Measured on the wheel that takes iso from 51 fives to THREE, and Dantley's Jazz '81 and King's Knicks '84 — the two fives his own iso rulings are named for — fall back to helio. At sum 0.90 (mid 0.15) it is 11 fives with the same two lost. The freed weight has to go back to the three terms he names, so the composite stays on the 0-100 axis ISO_BASE -6 and ISO_W_MAN 0.80 were fitted against.

AND WHERE IT GOES IS DECIDED BY HIS OWN PINNED READS, not by taste. Three splits of the freed 0.15 were measured, all summing to 1, all with mid 0.10. Feeding VOLUME first — either in the old 8:4:3 proportion (0.48 / 0.24 / 0.18) or rounded (0.45 / 0.25 / 0.20) — takes the THUNDER '25 off the pick-and-roll (iso 74.45 and 74.27 against pnr 74.19) and pushes iso to 81 and 75 fives. Leaving volume exactly where his earlier rounds put it and handing the freed weight to the two terms he names beside it holds every pinned read, and of the three that do (eff 0.30 / fd 0.20 -> 62 fives, eff 0.275 / fd 0.225 -> 64, eff 0.25 / fd 0.25 -> 70) the landed one has the smallest footprint on the wheel. It is also the only one that reads as a ladder: 0.40 / 0.30 / 0.20 / 0.10, in his own order, summing to 1 by construction.

'SMALL' IS BRACKETED FROM BOTH SIDES, with the rest of the ladder held in proportion. At mid 0.05 the bonus is too small to hold Leonard's RAPTORS '19 in the isolation and they fall to the pick-and-roll (66.54 against 66.88) — his ruling keeps them. At mid 0.20 it is large enough to take the THUNDER '25 off the roll (iso 74.33 against pnr 74.19) — a pinned read. The feasible window is 0.10 .. 0.15; 'small' is his word and takes the bottom of it, where the ladder also falls out, and where the mid term sits at half the smallest of the three core terms.
